assessment: One interaction hypothesis is supported as worth probing, not established as effective. Missing-part reports and short-partition confusion suggest a shared packing-to-unpacking interface; insertion difficulty and stage-specific time remain unresolved.

openings.claim: Cross an order-specific completeness template with an order-specific placement guide through shared partition codes. Workers verify each required loose partition against a reusable bench template; the matching customer diagram maps those same codes to positions in the ordered arrangement. This may permit verified kit packing with less workshop assembly while retaining unaided customer success.
openings.delta: A completeness template alone cannot explain placement, and a placement guide alone cannot establish that the correct pieces were packed. Their named interface is the common order-and-partition code carried from the bench check to the customer diagram. The predicted interaction is fewer wrong-piece placement attempts and help requests when both mechanisms use the same mapping.
openings.prediction: For otherwise identical kits, the combined condition should reduce incorrect placements and requests for help more than either component alone, with an interaction beyond their separate effects. Total workshop time may fall if avoided insertion time exceeds template checking time; customer insertion difficulty could defeat the benefit.
openings.probe: Use 12 of the 15 sample sets for an exploratory 2-by-2 comparison: completeness template present/absent and matching placement guide present/absent, with each of the three compartment counts represented in every condition. Hold kit presentation and components constant. Time selection, insertion, checking and packing separately; independently audit contents and exterior color. Allocate ten participants to first-use trials across conditions and record ordered-layout success, wrong placements and help requests. Separately compare workshop totals with the assembled workflow. This small probe can reject the mechanism but cannot establish the 60-unit success rates.
assumptions: Required parts, dimensions, capacity, selected counts and exterior colors remain unchanged; all joints remain dismantlable.
Codes can remain visible without weakening parts or creating placement ambiguity.
Templates and replacement diagrams fit the 500 initial and 0.40 recurring limits, and preparation fits the fixed delivery date; verify these before adoption.
Customers can assemble the supplied joints without workshop insertion; observed second attempts do not establish their cause.
